run.question: We noticed our metrics dashboard shows missing data. Can you analyze the app-189-metrics-timeseries index to find any gaps in the data collection? When did data stop being collected and when did it resume? Also, what was the last request ID before the gap started?

report.summary: The index app-189-metrics-timeseries is the only index in this Elasticsearch target and holds 42 documents, all with metric_name=cpu_usage, sampled once per hour at :45 from hosts server-1 through server-5. A complete enumeration of the index inside the authorized window (total 42, relation eq; earliest @timestamp 2026-11-21T18:45:00Z, latest 2026-11-23T17:45:00Z) shows exactly one internal break in the hourly cadence: the last sample before the break is 2026-11-23T07:45:00Z and the next is 2026-11-23T14:45:00Z, so the six hourly samples at 08:45, 09:45, 10:45, 11:45, 12:45 and 13:45 are missing and collection resumed at 2026-11-23T14:45:00Z. A query restricted to 2026-11-23T07:46:00Z-2026-11-23T14:44:59Z matched 0 documents, with per-hour buckets 08:00 through 14:00 all at doc_count 0. The last request_id recorded before the gap is REQ-37-8A4F2 (2026-11-23T07:45:00Z, host server-3, value 58.0); the first after the gap is REQ-2059-7454 (2026-11-23T14:45:00Z, host server-5, value 65.0). Nothing was returned before 2026-11-21T18:45:00Z, but index metadata reports creation.date 2026-11-23T17:46:40Z with docs.deleted 42, so the earlier absence cannot be read as a collection gap and retention history is not observable. What interrupted collection between 08:45 and 13:45 on 2026-11-23 is not established: no collector workload or configuration object tied to this index was found (the Prometheus metric-name lookup for '*189*' returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and a pod filter on name/labels/annotations containing '189' matched nothing), so the cause remains unknown rather than identified.

claims.text: app-189-metrics-timeseries is the only index present and contains 42 documents; a query of the whole authorized window returned all of them (total 42, relation eq), with @timestamp ranging from 2026-11-21T18:45:00Z to 2026-11-23T17:45:00Z, every document carrying metric_name=cpu_usage and host among server-1..server-5.

The hourly samples (one per hour, each at :45) contain one break on 2026-11-23: the sample at 2026-11-23T07:45:00Z is followed directly by 2026-11-23T14:45:00Z, so the expected samples at 08:45, 09:45, 10:45, 11:45, 12:45 and 13:45 are missing.

A search restricted to 2026-11-23T07:46:00Z-2026-11-23T14:44:59Z matched 0 documents (total relation eq, value 0) and its per-hour date_histogram buckets for 08:00, 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 13:00 and 14:00 each show doc_count 0, confirming no collection in that interval.

The last document before the gap is @timestamp 2026-11-23T07:45:00Z with request_id REQ-37-8A4F2, host server-3, metric_name cpu_usage, value 58.0; the first document after the gap is @timestamp 2026-11-23T14:45:00Z with request_id REQ-2059-7454, host server-5, value 65.0.

Across the 42 returned documents, request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 is the only value that does not follow the REQ-<digits>-<digits> pattern used by the other 41 documents; no evidence in this run ties that formatting difference to the collection gap.

The index reports creation.date 2026-11-23T17:46:40.148Z with docs.count 42 and docs.deleted 42, i.e. index metadata observed at query time describes an index (re)created at 17:46:40Z, after every document it holds; therefore the absence of documents before 2026-11-21T18:45:00Z cannot be read as a collection outage or as retention evidence.

The 2026-11-23T08:45-13:45 gap is most consistent with the metrics writer or collector for this index not emitting or not ingesting documents for about six hours, since the hourly cadence before and after the gap is uninterrupted and the metric values stay in their normal 20-77 range on both sides; the producing agent itself was not observed, so this remains unverified.

To attribute the gap, check the collector or agent that writes app-189-metrics-timeseries (its logs and restart history around 2026-11-23T08:45-14:45) and the ingest pipeline or shard state for that index during the gap; neither is covered by the sources queried here.

gaps: The cause of the 2026-11-23T08:45-13:45 collection gap is unknown: no evidence in this run identifies the writer, its configuration, a restart or an ingest failure. The environment exposes no change-history integration (listed as not_integrated: change_history), so change records cannot be consulted.

No Kubernetes object tied to this index was found: the pod query across all namespaces filtered on name/labels/annotations containing '189' returned a no_data view (59d2a716-952d-4e01-a4a4-e8a8bacde256-t1:c9c5718b-5290-411d-b145-030714d49d2b), which shows only that the filter matched nothing at query time, not that no such object existed during the gap.
A Prometheus lookup for metric names matching '.*189.*|.*metric.*timeseries.*' returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so Prometheus-side collection signals for an app-189 exporter were not checked.
Elasticsearch holds only app-189-metrics-timeseries; there is no second index, alias or rollover target to show whether the same hourly series continued elsewhere during the gap.

Whether data existed before 2026-11-21T18:45:00Z (collection start, retention, or index recreation) is unknown; the index metadata's creation.date (2026-11-23T17:46:40Z) postdates all its documents, so retention history is not observable from this target.
next_steps: Query the agent or collector logs and restart history for the writer of app-189-metrics-timeseries over 2026-11-23T07:45:00Z-2026-11-23T14:45:00Z to determine whether it stopped, was throttled or failed to ingest.
Check Elasticsearch ingest/pipeline statistics and shard allocation history for app-189-metrics-timeseries across the gap window.
If a Prometheus exporter or scrape job for app-189 exists, verify its scrape targets and up/error series once the Prometheus source is reachable, to distinguish producer outage from ingest outage.
